title: Rank-zero and rank-one Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer theory, Part II: the p-converse
summary: The squarefree-level converse for modular abelian varieties is obtained from a rational Selmer localization criterion over an imaginary quadratic field. Anticyclotomic reverse divisibility and finite-error control force a nonzero p-adic logarithm of a normalized Heegner point. Existing height and descent theorems then recover analytic rank one, arithmetic rank and finite Tate–Shafarevich groups. The rational rank-one, mod-p and rank-zero consequences retain Skinner’s local hypotheses.
readme: See research/blueprint/readmes/RankOneConverse.md for exact conventions, targets, APIs, discriminating tests, source locators and supplier boundaries. This Part II assembles the converse; its parent owns the forward BSD direction. Theorem D stays with ArithmeticStatistics ST.4. The seven layers are planned at target granularity and remain open at the precise supplier requests recorded in the packet.

stages.title: Squarefree local data and Heegner normalization
stages.description: Translate the squarefree local epsilon factors into Skinner’s modular and indefinite quaternionic cases. Prove residual irreducibility after quadratic restriction. Normalize the Hecke-projected CM divisor, its rational Hodge representative and the transferred differential; import the curves, Jacobians, projectors and CM descent.

stages.title: Rational Selmer localization and strict kernels
stages.description: Define the rank-one localization criterion on an actual linear restriction map. Assemble the GL₂-type Kummer/Sha and quadratic comparisons, repair componentwise eigenlogarithm localization, compute the two-dimensional semilocal image and prove strict/one-sided kernel vanishing. Import ordinary modular parity.

stages.title: Anticyclotomic divisibility and augmentation control
stages.description: Instantiate the inverse-tautological anticyclotomic Selmer deformation with the inertia-strict condition at one p-adic prime. Match integral imprimitive analytic functions and character conventions. Specialize the ordinary Wan Fitting bound with exact control and divisorial closure. Prove that augmentation vanishing produces a nonzero rational one-sided class.

stages.title: The quadratic-field p-converse
stages.description: Identify the same normalized point in the complex height and squared-log formulas, including the actual-point eigenlogarithm repair. Assemble Skinner Theorem B with precisely conditions (a)–(e), analytic orders 1 and d, rank d and entire Sha finiteness through the full forward supplier.

stages.title: The rational rank-one converse
stages.description: Choose auxiliary imaginary quadratic fields retaining a residual-ramified nonsplit prime and a nonzero twist value. Apply the corrected arithmetic-localization criterion to prove Skinner Theorem A for modular abelian varieties and Theorem A′ for semistable elliptic curves, with the stated odd-prime reduction alternatives.

stages.title: The mod-p Selmer criterion
stages.description: Turn the mod-p Selmer line and torsion-avoidance hypothesis into rational localization using the perfect alternating pairing, not square cardinality alone. Produce an odd residual-ramified prime at the given p by level lowering. Prove Skinner Theorem C and export it to the statistical owner of Theorem D.

stages.title: The rank-zero converse
stages.description: Use a locally prescribed derivative-nonvanishing twist, rather than a sign-only argument, to produce rank-d base change from rational rank zero. Apply Theorem B and subtract the twist analytic order to prove Skinner Theorem E with its original squarefree/local-type hypotheses.
